name: freight claims

product.purpose: Prepare source-linked claim packets with carrier-specific evidence checklists, filing windows, and response-date tracking for customer-confirmed freight loss, damage, or shortage.
product.publication: The first ShipStation app listing is owner-reviewed. Glacier reads ShipStation only and never submits or sends a carrier claim.
product.billing: Prepare a 20–30% contingency invoice draft only after recovery is confirmed; customer agreement and owner approval are required before billing.

schedules.purpose: Read ShipStation shipment records daily and save possible exceptions for customer confirmation.
Collect local 30- and 120-day claim-status follow-ups from customer-confirmed carrier receipt dates; LTL regulatory milestones are noted only when 49 CFR Part 370 applies.

your_steps.title: Connect ShipStation or add a shipments export
your_steps.detail: Choose either option. For automatic ShipStation reads, the owner checks the Gold plan requirement and current quota, saves the read-only API key in Glacier's keychain, explicitly enables polling, runs the connection check, and reviews the first shipment list. If the account cannot use the API, the owner downloads a Shipments or Orders CSV and places it in this computer's freight-claims/incoming folder; the daily check uses the newest CSV automatically. Before routine use, review and approve the first ten distinct claim packets against source documents, carrier terms, carrier-specific evidence guidance, and insurance status. Glacier never creates accounts, changes shipments, or publishes listings.

secrets.name: shipstation_api_key
secrets.label: ShipStation API key (only for API access)

your_steps.title: Review, file, and respond to each claim
your_steps.when: After the shipper reviews a prepared packet
your_steps.detail: For each claim, the shipper confirms details, supplies or signs owner-approved authorization, reviews and files the packet with the carrier, then records the carrier receipt/reference and any response or recovery date. Glacier never signs or files for the shipper. If a full-release settlement arrives, the shipper explicitly accepts or declines; acceptance closes the claim and decline leaves it active. The owner approves any invoice draft before it is sent or charged.

launch_gates: Owner reviews the first ShipStation app listing.
Owner reviews the first ten claim packets.
No carrier message, filing, signature, invoice, or payment is sent by Glacier without an exact approval step; real carrier submission remains with the shipper.
